notes.heading: 想 — want to vs. think about / miss
notes.body: 想 xiǎng is two different words. Before another verb it is a modal verb meaning "want to / would like to" (negated with 不想). As an ordinary verb with a noun or person after it, it means "to think about" or "to miss". Context and what follows 想 tell you which one you have.

examples.english: I want to eat rice.

notes.heading: …就行 — that's enough, that will do
notes.body: Put 就行 jiù xíng after a condition or an action to say that it is enough and nothing more is needed. The tone is relaxed: a simple condition is sufficient. It is often used when answering "what do you need?" or "is it hard?".

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen shuō Zhōngwén jiù xíng.

examples.english: Not too hard — preparing carefully is enough.

notes.heading: 怕 — to fear, to worry that
notes.body: 怕 pà can take a noun (be afraid of something) or a whole clause (be worried that something will happen). In the lesson dialogue, 你不怕摔就行 uses it together with 就行: as long as you aren't afraid of falling, that is enough.

notes.heading: 几 — how many vs. several
notes.body: In a question 几 jǐ asks "how many / which number" for small numbers (dates, weekdays, family members, a child's age) and is followed by a measure word. In a statement 几 means "a few, several", and 十几 means "more than ten" (eleven to nineteen).

examples.english: What day of the week is it today?

notes.heading: 跟…一起 — together with someone
notes.body: 跟 gēn means "with" and introduces the person you do something with. Together with 一起 yìqǐ it forms 跟 + person + 一起 + verb, placed before the main verb. The whole sentence is a serial verb sentence: one subject, several actions.

examples.chinese: 我跟同学一起去郊区滑雪了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ gēn tóngxué yìqǐ qù jiāoqū huáxuě le.
examples.english: I went skiing in the suburbs together with my classmates.

examples.english: I'd like to go together with you.

notes.heading: 怎么没…？ — why didn't…?
notes.body: 怎么 before 没 + verb asks why something that was expected did not happen, usually with a note of surprise. Compare 你怎么走？ (how do you go?) with 你怎么没走？ (why didn't you go?). A typical answer gives a reason or reports the new situation with 了.

selfCheck.q: Is this a pivotal sentence (兼语句)? 他去学校跑步了。
selfCheck.a: No — one subject (他) does both actions, so it is a serial verb sentence 连动句. (Tā qù xuéxiào pǎobù le.)

selfCheck.a: Yes — 你 is the object of 请 and the subject of 看. (Wǒ qǐng nǐ kàn diànyǐng.)

selfCheck.q: Is this a pivotal sentence (兼语句)? 妈妈要求我每天十点睡觉。

selfCheck.q: Is this a pivotal sentence (兼语句)? 周末我们一起去王老师家吃饭。
selfCheck.a: No — 我们 does both 去 and 吃饭, so it is a 连动句. (Zhōumò wǒmen yìqǐ qù Wáng lǎoshī jiā chī fàn.)

selfCheck.q: Is this a pivotal sentence (兼语句)? 小丽来医院看一个同学。

selfCheck.q: Rewrite as a 吗 question, two affirmative-negative questions, and a negative sentence (pronouns adjusted): 我吃早饭了。

notes.body: Action counters follow the verb, just like 次: Verb + number + counter. 遍 means doing something once through from start to finish, such as reading or writing it all the way, and 趟 counts trips that involve going somewhere and back. 回 is an informal stand-in for 次, and 下 marks a quick, light action such as knocking or clicking.

notes.body: To describe a dose or a routine, give the frequency first and then the amount each time: 一天三次，一次两片. notes.heading: 还是 — the third meaning: still
notes.body: Besides 'or' in choice questions and 'had better' with 吧, 还是 can mean 'still': things are unchanged, or someone carries on in spite of the circumstances. It goes before the verb or adjective in a plain statement. The sentence type tells you which meaning you have.

notes.heading: 怎么 — how, what happened, and why
notes.body: 怎么 changes its job with its position. At the end of a sentence, 怎么样 asks how something is and 怎么了 asks what happened to it. Before a verb, usually with 不, 没 or 还不, 怎么 asks 'why' with a hint of surprise because you have noticed something unexpected. The neutral way to ask for a reason is still 为什么.

notes.heading: 了 — life changes and the start of an illness
notes.body: A sentence-final 了 announces that a situation has changed, so it fits changes of job, health or life stage alike. Add 已经 (already) or 最近 (lately) before the verb if you like, but keep 了 at the end. Illnesses that have just begun, such as 感冒, 发烧 and 过敏, are normally reported with 了, while a pain like 头疼 simply describes how you feel now.

notes.body: Look at what comes next. Before an adjective or verb phrase that describes an unwelcome state, use 有点儿: 今天有点儿冷. After an adjective, or before a noun, use 一点儿: 小一点儿的, 加一点儿盐. To say you have a small amount of something, use 有一点儿 plus the noun: 我有一点儿钱.

selfCheck.q: What's the difference between 一次 and 第一次?

selfCheck.a: 会 = learned skill; 能 = ability or circumstance; 可以 = permission.

selfCheck.q: What's the difference between 次, 遍 and 趟?
selfCheck.a: 次 simply counts how many times; 遍 means once through from start to finish (读一遍, read it through); 趟 means a trip there and back (去一趟, make one trip).

selfCheck.q: How do you ask "Why aren't you up yet?"

selfCheck.q: What does 还是 mean in 我还是爱你的？

notes.heading: Opposite words — 反义词
notes.body: Pairs of opposites are an easy way to double your adjective vocabulary, so learn them together and use them in contrast sentences such as 他个子很高，他弟弟很矮. When you do not know the true opposite you can often fall back on 不 + the adjective — 不好 for 很差, 不忙 for 闲 — but the real opposite sounds more natural. A bare adjective without 很 — as in 他高，他弟弟矮 — already sounds like a deliberate contrast.

notes.heading: 想 vs 要 — wanting, ordering and planning

selfCheck.a: 这个蛋糕不太甜，我很喜欢。(Zhège dàngāo bú tài tián, wǒ hěn xǐhuan.)

selfCheck.q: Reply to “我怕狗。” (I'm afraid of dogs.)
selfCheck.a: 别担心，它很乖的。(Bié dānxīn, tā hěn guāi de.) — Don't worry, it's very well-behaved.

selfCheck.q: Reply to “服务员，请给我一杯咖啡。小丽，你喝什么？” (Waiter, a coffee for me please. Xiao Li, what will you have?)
selfCheck.a: 我想喝红茶。(Wǒ xiǎng hē hóngchá.) — I'd like black tea.

selfCheck.q: Reply to “他个子真高！” (He is so tall!)
selfCheck.a: 是啊，一米八呢。(Shì a, yì mǐ bā ne.) — Yes, he's one metre eighty!

selfCheck.q: Reply to “今天我们自己做水果披萨，怎么样？” (How about making fruit pizza ourselves today?)
selfCheck.a: 好主意！(Hǎo zhǔyi!) — Good idea!

selfCheck.q: Reply to “你有什么爱好？” (What are your hobbies?)
selfCheck.a: 我喜欢看电影和旅游。(Wǒ xǐhuan kàn diànyǐng hé lǚyóu.) — I like watching films and travelling.

selfCheck.q: Reply to “老公，我想吃蛋糕，怕你不同意。” (Darling, I'd like to eat cake, but I'm afraid you won't agree.)
selfCheck.a: 没问题。今天特价，很便宜。(Méi wèntí. Jīntiān tèjià, hěn piányi.) — No problem. It's on special today and very cheap.

selfCheck.q: Reply to “你去过上海吗？” (Have you ever been to Shanghai?)
selfCheck.a: 没去过，我想去。(Méi qù guo, wǒ xiǎng qù.) — No, but I'd like to.

selfCheck.q: Reply to “一共八十块，请问您怎么付？” (That's eighty yuan in total; how would you like to pay?)
selfCheck.a: 刷卡。(Shuā kǎ.) — By card.

selfCheck.q: Passage “An International Student in China”: 大卫是哪国人？（A. 中国人 B. 美国人 C. 英国人）
selfCheck.a: B. 美国人。(Měiguó rén.) — David is American.

selfCheck.q: Passage “An International Student in China”: 大卫没去过哪个城市？（A. 上海 B. 杭州 C. 西安）
selfCheck.a: C. 西安。(Xī'ān.) — He has been to Shanghai and Hangzhou but not yet to Xi'an.

selfCheck.q: Passage “An International Student in China”: 大卫周末常常做什么？（A. 去医院 B. 喝咖啡、散步 C. 上课）
selfCheck.a: B. 喝咖啡、散步。(Hē kāfēi, sànbù.) — He often drinks coffee with friends or goes for a walk.

selfCheck.q: Free talk: 你喜欢的一个地方。(Describe a place that you like.)
selfCheck.a: Sample answer: 我喜欢上海。那儿很漂亮，吃的东西也很多。(Wǒ xǐhuan Shànghǎi. Nàr hěn piàoliang, chī de dōngxi yě hěn duō.) — I like Shanghai. It is beautiful and there is a lot to eat.

selfCheck.q: Insert 还 into: 我会中国功夫。
selfCheck.a: 我还会中国功夫。(Wǒ hái huì Zhōngguó gōngfu.)

selfCheck.q: Insert 得 into: 他的法语说不错。
selfCheck.a: 他的法语说得不错。(Tā de Fǎyǔ shuō de bú cuò.)

selfCheck.q: Insert 都 into: 爸妈不是医生？
selfCheck.a: 爸妈都不是医生？(Bàmā dōu bú shì yīshēng?) — 都 comes before 不: neither of them is a doctor. (爸妈不都是医生？ would mean "aren't both doctors?")

selfCheck.q: Insert 不 into: 你工作忙忙？
selfCheck.a: 你工作忙不忙？(Nǐ gōngzuò máng bù máng?)

selfCheck.q: Insert 了 into: 妈妈吃完饭。
selfCheck.a: 妈妈吃完饭了。(Māma chī wán fàn le.)

selfCheck.q: Insert 过 into: 你去纽约吗？
selfCheck.a: 你去过纽约吗？(Nǐ qù guo Niǔyuē ma?)

selfCheck.q: Fill the blank （平时 / 每天 / 没 / 一起 / 多少 / 除了 / 在 / 一般 / 跟 / 不过）: 我朋友____都很忙。
selfCheck.a: 我朋友平时都很忙。(Wǒ péngyou píngshí dōu hěn máng.)

selfCheck.q: Fill the blank （平时 / 每天 / 没 / 一起 / 多少 / 除了 / 在 / 一般 / 跟 / 不过）: 李老师____家吗？
selfCheck.a: 李老师在家吗？(Lǐ lǎoshī zài jiā ma?)

selfCheck.q: Fill the blank （平时 / 每天 / 没 / 一起 / 多少 / 除了 / 在 / 一般 / 跟 / 不过）: 他的手机号码是____？
selfCheck.a: 他的手机号码是多少？(Tā de shǒujī hàomǎ shì duōshao?)

selfCheck.q: Fill the blank （平时 / 每天 / 没 / 一起 / 多少 / 除了 / 在 / 一般 / 跟 / 不过）: 我____时间去买东西。
selfCheck.a: 我没时间去买东西。(Wǒ méi shíjiān qù mǎi dōngxi.)

selfCheck.q: Fill the blank （平时 / 每天 / 没 / 一起 / 多少 / 除了 / 在 / 一般 / 跟 / 不过）: 我____晚上学习汉语。
selfCheck.a: 我每天晚上学习汉语。(Wǒ měi tiān wǎnshang xuéxí Hànyǔ.)

selfCheck.q: Fill the blank （平时 / 每天 / 没 / 一起 / 多少 / 除了 / 在 / 一般 / 跟 / 不过）: 你____几点睡觉？
selfCheck.a: 你一般几点睡觉？(Nǐ yìbān jǐ diǎn shuìjiào?)

selfCheck.q: Fill the blank （平时 / 每天 / 没 / 一起 / 多少 / 除了 / 在 / 一般 / 跟 / 不过）: 我喜欢____朋友聊天儿。
selfCheck.a: 我喜欢跟朋友聊天儿。(Wǒ xǐhuan gēn péngyou liáotiānr.)

selfCheck.q: Fill the blank （平时 / 每天 / 没 / 一起 / 多少 / 除了 / 在 / 一般 / 跟 / 不过）: 我们常常____学习汉语。
selfCheck.a: 我们常常一起学习汉语。(Wǒmen chángcháng yìqǐ xuéxí Hànyǔ.)

selfCheck.q: Fill the blank （平时 / 每天 / 没 / 一起 / 多少 / 除了 / 在 / 一般 / 跟 / 不过）: 我会说汉语，____说得不太好。
selfCheck.a: 我会说汉语，不过说得不太好。(Wǒ huì shuō Hànyǔ, búguò shuō de bú tài hǎo.)

selfCheck.q: Fill the blank （平时 / 每天 / 没 / 一起 / 多少 / 除了 / 在 / 一般 / 跟 / 不过）: ____老板，大家都在忙。
selfCheck.a: 除了老板，大家都在忙。(Chúle lǎobǎn, dàjiā dōu zài máng.)

selfCheck.q: Reply to “你想去泰国还是马来西亚？” (Do you want to go to Thailand or Malaysia?)
selfCheck.a: 我哪儿都不想去，我想在家。(Wǒ nǎr dōu bù xiǎng qù, wǒ xiǎng zài jiā.) — I don't want to go anywhere; I want to stay at home.

selfCheck.q: Reply to “除了唱歌，你还有什么特长？” (Besides singing, what other special skills do you have?)
selfCheck.a: 我还会滑雪。(Wǒ hái huì huáxuě.) — I can also ski.

selfCheck.q: Reply to “爸妈身体怎么样？” (How is your parents' health?)
selfCheck.a: 都很好，放心吧。(Dōu hěn hǎo, fàngxīn ba.) — They are both well, don't worry.

selfCheck.q: Reply to “我看见小丽的男朋友了。” (I saw Xiao Li's boyfriend.)
selfCheck.a: 怎么样，帅吗？(Zěnmeyàng, shuài ma?) — Well? Is he handsome?

selfCheck.q: Reply to “请问，你也住在这儿吗？” (Excuse me, do you live here too?)
selfCheck.a: 我住十层，很高兴认识你。(Wǒ zhù shí céng, hěn gāoxìng rènshi nǐ.) — I live on the tenth floor; nice to meet you.

selfCheck.q: Reply to “假期我们一起去上海吧。” (Let's go to Shanghai together in the holidays.)
selfCheck.a: 我也想去。可是我要加班。(Wǒ yě xiǎng qù. Kěshì wǒ yào jiābān.) — I'd like to go too, but I have to work overtime.

selfCheck.q: Reply to “我最近养了一只小狗，特别可爱。” (I've recently got a puppy; it's especially cute.)
selfCheck.a: 它叫什么名字？(Tā jiào shénme míngzi?) — What is its name?

selfCheck.q: Reply to “你去过的地方真多啊。” (You've been to so many places!)
selfCheck.a: 我喜欢旅行，旅行让我快乐。(Wǒ xǐhuan lǚxíng, lǚxíng ràng wǒ kuàilè.) — I like travelling; travelling makes me happy.

selfCheck.q: Passage “My Roommate”: 我的同屋做什么工作？（A. 中国人 B. 学生 C. 汽车公司）
selfCheck.a: C. 汽车公司。(Qìchē gōngsī.) — He works at a car company.

selfCheck.q: Passage “My Roommate”: 他们经常在家做饭。（A. 不知道 B. 对 C. 不对）
selfCheck.a: C. 不对。(Bú duì.) — On ordinary days they eat at school or out; they only cook at home when they are off.

selfCheck.q: Passage “My Roommate”: 休息的时候，我和同屋做什么？（A. 玩游戏 B. 喝咖啡、散步 C. 做饭）
selfCheck.a: C. 做饭。(Zuò fàn.) — They cook at home and chat while eating.

selfCheck.q: Put in order: 不太 / 游泳 / 得 / 他 / 游 / 好
selfCheck.a: 他游泳游得不太好。(Tā yóuyǒng yóu de bú tài hǎo.)

selfCheck.q: Put in order: 打 / 妈妈 / 会 / 篮球 / 不
selfCheck.a: 妈妈不会打篮球。(Māma bú huì dǎ lánqiú.)

selfCheck.q: Put in order: 跳舞 / 非常 / 好 / 他的 / 跳得 / 女儿
selfCheck.a: 他的女儿跳舞跳得非常好。(Tā de nǚ'ér tiàowǔ tiào de fēicháng hǎo.)

selfCheck.q: Put in order: 吗 / 十二 / 是 / 你 / 住 / 层
selfCheck.a: 你是住十二层吗？(Nǐ shì zhù shí'èr céng ma?) — 你是住在十二层吗？ is also fine.

selfCheck.q: Put in order: 辣 / 饭馆 / 这 / 都 / 家 / 菜 / 的 / 很
selfCheck.a: 这家饭馆的菜都很辣。(Zhè jiā fànguǎn de cài dōu hěn là.)

selfCheck.q: Put in order: 工作 / 了 / 在 / 他 / 年 / 西餐厅 / 两 / 那家
selfCheck.a: 他在那家西餐厅工作了两年。(Tā zài nà jiā xīcāntīng gōngzuò le liǎng nián.)

selfCheck.q: Put in order: 米饭 / 想 / 还是 / 吃 / 面条 / 你
selfCheck.a: 你想吃米饭还是面条？(Nǐ xiǎng chī mǐfàn háishi miàntiáo?)

selfCheck.q: Put in order: 刷卡 / 您 / 还是 / 现金 / 付
selfCheck.a: 您刷卡还是付现金？(Nín shuā kǎ háishi fù xiànjīn?) — 您付现金还是刷卡？ also works.

selfCheck.q: Put in order: 喝 / 我 / 咖啡 / 想 / 不
selfCheck.a: 我不想喝咖啡。(Wǒ bù xiǎng hē kāfēi.)

selfCheck.q: Put in order: 特价 / 蛋糕 / 这 / 今天 / 种
selfCheck.a: 今天这种蛋糕特价。(Jīntiān zhè zhǒng dàngāo tèjià.)

selfCheck.q: Put in order: 大杯 / 要 / 红茶 / 他 / 了
selfCheck.a: 他要了大杯红茶。(Tā yào le dàbēi hóngchá.)

selfCheck.q: Put in order: 房间 / 住 / 小丽 / 不 / 一零三
selfCheck.a: 小丽不住一零三房间。(Xiǎo Lì bú zhù yāo líng sān fángjiān.)

selfCheck.q: Put in order: 头发 / 长 / 你 / 真
selfCheck.a: 你头发真长。(Nǐ tóufa zhēn cháng.)

selfCheck.q: Put in order: 怎么样 / 这 / 餐厅 / 家 / 中国
selfCheck.a: 这家中国餐厅怎么样？(Zhè jiā Zhōngguó cāntīng zěnmeyàng?)

selfCheck.q: Put in order: 水果 / 便宜 / 都 / 的 / 这儿 / 很
selfCheck.a: 这儿的水果都很便宜。(Zhèr de shuǐguǒ dōu hěn piányi.)

selfCheck.q: Put in order: 买 / 想 / 那个 / 的 / 我 / 好看 / 杯子
selfCheck.a: 我想买那个好看的杯子。(Wǒ xiǎng mǎi nàge hǎokàn de bēizi.)

selfCheck.q: Put in order: 有 / 星期一 / 你 / 吗 / 时间
selfCheck.a: 星期一你有时间吗？(Xīngqīyī nǐ yǒu shíjiān ma?) — 你星期一有时间吗？ also works.

selfCheck.q: Put in order: 三 / 种 / 会 / 老师 / 语言 / 说
selfCheck.a: 老师会说三种语言。(Lǎoshī huì shuō sān zhǒng yǔyán.)

selfCheck.q: Put in order: 是 / 我的 / 看 / 爱好 / 电影
selfCheck.a: 我的爱好是看电影。(Wǒ de àihào shì kàn diànyǐng.)

selfCheck.q: Put in order: 什么 / 除了 / 意大利面 / 还 / 吃 / 你
selfCheck.a: 除了意大利面，你还吃什么？(Chúle Yìdàlì miàn, nǐ hái chī shénme?)

selfCheck.q: Put in order: 他 / 好 / 不太 / 唱歌 / 得 / 唱
selfCheck.a: 他唱歌唱得不太好。(Tā chànggē chàng de bú tài hǎo.)

selfCheck.q: Put in order: 不错 / 爸爸 / 打得 / 网球
selfCheck.a: 爸爸网球打得不错。(Bàba wǎngqiú dǎ de bú cuò.)

selfCheck.q: Put in order: 喜欢 / 一起 / 小明 / 游戏 / 和 / 打 / 朋友
selfCheck.a: 小明喜欢和朋友一起打游戏。(Xiǎo Míng xǐhuan hé péngyou yìqǐ dǎ yóuxì.)

selfCheck.q: Write the opposite of 高.
selfCheck.a: 矮 (ǎi) — short

selfCheck.q: Write the opposite of 瘦.
selfCheck.a: 胖 (pàng) — fat

selfCheck.q: Write the opposite of 长.
selfCheck.a: 短 (duǎn) — short

selfCheck.q: Write the opposite of 小.
selfCheck.a: 大 (dà) — big

selfCheck.q: Write the opposite of 便宜.
selfCheck.a: 贵 (guì) — expensive

selfCheck.q: Write the opposite of 很好.
selfCheck.a: 很差 (hěn chà) — very poor; 不好 (bù hǎo) is also acceptable

selfCheck.q: Write the opposite of 忙.
selfCheck.a: 闲 (xián) — free; 不忙 (bù máng) is also acceptable

selfCheck.q: Choose the reply （我要一杯茶 / 我不想吃，我想吃面条儿 / 我不会 / 我住一零二 / 我喜欢旅游 / 我还没去过呢） to “您想喝点儿什么？” (What would you like to drink?)
selfCheck.a: 我要一杯茶。(Wǒ yào yì bēi chá.)

selfCheck.q: Choose the reply （我要一杯茶 / 我不想吃，我想吃面条儿 / 我不会 / 我住一零二 / 我喜欢旅游 / 我还没去过呢） to “吃比萨，怎么样？” (How about pizza?)
selfCheck.a: 我不想吃，我想吃面条儿。(Wǒ bù xiǎng chī, wǒ xiǎng chī miàntiáor.)

selfCheck.q: Choose the reply （我要一杯茶 / 我不想吃，我想吃面条儿 / 我不会 / 我住一零二 / 我喜欢旅游 / 我还没去过呢） to “你会唱汉语歌吗？” (Can you sing Chinese songs?)
selfCheck.a: 我不会。(Wǒ bú huì.)

selfCheck.q: Choose the reply （我要一杯茶 / 我不想吃，我想吃面条儿 / 我不会 / 我住一零二 / 我喜欢旅游 / 我还没去过呢） to “你住哪儿？” (Where do you live?)
selfCheck.a: 我住一零二。(Wǒ zhù yāo líng èr.) — I live in room 102.

selfCheck.q: Choose the reply （我要一杯茶 / 我不想吃，我想吃面条儿 / 我不会 / 我住一零二 / 我喜欢旅游 / 我还没去过呢） to “你有什么爱好？” (What are your hobbies?)
selfCheck.a: 我喜欢旅游。(Wǒ xǐhuan lǚyóu.)

selfCheck.q: Choose the reply （我要一杯茶 / 我不想吃，我想吃面条儿 / 我不会 / 我住一零二 / 我喜欢旅游 / 我还没去过呢） to “你去过上海吗？” (Have you ever been to Shanghai?)
selfCheck.a: 我还没去过呢。(Wǒ hái méi qù guo ne.)

selfCheck.q: Fill the blank （会 / 想 / 得 / 真 / 过）: 我歌唱____不太好。
selfCheck.a: 我歌唱得不太好。(Wǒ gē chàng de bú tài hǎo.)

selfCheck.q: Fill the blank （会 / 想 / 得 / 真 / 过）: 她身材____好！
selfCheck.a: 她身材真好！(Tā shēncái zhēn hǎo!)

selfCheck.q: Fill the blank （会 / 想 / 得 / 真 / 过）: 我以前去____上海。
selfCheck.a: 我以前去过上海。(Wǒ yǐqián qù guo Shànghǎi.)

selfCheck.q: Fill the blank （会 / 想 / 得 / 真 / 过）: 我____说四种语言。
selfCheck.a: 我会说四种语言。(Wǒ huì shuō sì zhǒng yǔyán.)

selfCheck.q: Fill the blank （会 / 想 / 得 / 真 / 过）: 我不____吃包子，咱们吃比萨吧。
selfCheck.a: 我不想吃包子，咱们吃比萨吧。(Wǒ bù xiǎng chī bāozi, zánmen chī bǐsà ba.)

selfCheck.q: Fill the blank （都 / 不过 / 最近 / 还是 / 除了）: 请问，您要大杯____小杯？
selfCheck.a: 请问，您要大杯还是小杯？(Qǐngwèn, nín yào dàbēi háishi xiǎobēi?)

selfCheck.q: Fill the blank （都 / 不过 / 最近 / 还是 / 除了）: 我____每天吃饺子。
selfCheck.a: 我最近每天吃饺子。(Wǒ zuìjìn měi tiān chī jiǎozi.)

selfCheck.q: Fill the blank （都 / 不过 / 最近 / 还是 / 除了）: ____这些，你还有什么特长？
selfCheck.a: 除了这些，你还有什么特长？(Chúle zhèxiē, nǐ hái yǒu shénme tècháng?)

selfCheck.q: Fill the blank （都 / 不过 / 最近 / 还是 / 除了）: 我喜欢篮球，____不会打。
selfCheck.a: 我喜欢篮球，不过不会打。(Wǒ xǐhuan lánqiú, búguò bú huì dǎ.)

selfCheck.q: Fill the blank （都 / 不过 / 最近 / 还是 / 除了）: 这些我____不喜欢。
selfCheck.a: 这些我都不喜欢。(Zhèxiē wǒ dōu bù xǐhuan.)

selfCheck.q: Answer in your own words: 你喜欢吃什么？ (What do you like to eat?)
selfCheck.a: Sample answer: 我喜欢吃饺子和面条儿。(Wǒ xǐhuan chī jiǎozi hé miàntiáor.)

selfCheck.q: Answer in your own words: 你喜欢刷卡还是付现金？ (Do you prefer paying by card or in cash?)
selfCheck.a: Sample answer: 我喜欢刷卡。(Wǒ xǐhuan shuā kǎ.)

selfCheck.q: Answer in your own words: 你爸妈身体怎么样？ (How is your parents' health?)
selfCheck.a: Sample answer: 他们身体都很好。(Tāmen shēntǐ dōu hěn hǎo.)

selfCheck.q: Answer in your own words: 你住哪儿？ (Where do you live?)
selfCheck.a: Sample answer: 我住在上海。(Wǒ zhù zài Shànghǎi.)

selfCheck.q: Answer in your own words: 你喜欢小狗吗？ (Do you like puppies?)
selfCheck.a: Sample answer: 我很喜欢小狗，它们很可爱。(Wǒ hěn xǐhuan xiǎo gǒu, tāmen hěn kě'ài.)

selfCheck.q: Answer in your own words: 你有什么爱好？ (What are your hobbies?)
selfCheck.a: Sample answer: 我的爱好是看电影和旅游。(Wǒ de àihào shì kàn diànyǐng hé lǚyóu.)

selfCheck.q: Answer in your own words: 你的特长是什么？ (What is your special skill?)
selfCheck.a: Sample answer: 我会唱歌，还会游泳。(Wǒ huì chànggē, hái huì yóuyǒng.)

selfCheck.q: Answer in your own words: 你会说什么语言？ (Which languages do you speak?)
selfCheck.a: Sample answer: 我会说英语和汉语。(Wǒ huì shuō Yīngyǔ hé Hànyǔ.)

selfCheck.q: Answer in your own words: 你游泳游得怎么样？ (How well do you swim?)
selfCheck.a: Sample answer: 我游泳游得不错。(Wǒ yóuyǒng yóu de bú cuò.)

selfCheck.q: Answer in your own words: 你都去过什么好玩儿的地方？ (What fun places have you been to?)
selfCheck.a: Sample answer: 我去过上海和杭州。(Wǒ qù guo Shànghǎi hé Hángzhōu.)

selfCheck.q: Speaking prompt: 你想吃披萨还是面条？为什么？(Would you rather eat pizza or noodles? Why?)
selfCheck.a: Sample answer: 我想吃面条，因为我喜欢吃辣的。(Wǒ xiǎng chī miàntiáo, yīnwèi wǒ xǐhuan chī là de.)

selfCheck.q: Speaking prompt: 说说你的一次旅行经历或者新的旅行计划。(Talk about a trip you have taken or a new travel plan. Starters: 我想去…… / 我去过……)
selfCheck.a: Sample answer: 我去过杭州，我觉得那儿很漂亮。我想假期去西安。(Wǒ qù guo Hángzhōu, wǒ juéde nàr hěn piàoliang. Wǒ xiǎng jiàqī qù Xī'ān.)

selfCheck.q: Fill the blank （你 / 饿）: ____好！
selfCheck.a: 你好！(Nǐ hǎo!)

selfCheck.q: Fill the blank （很 / 是）: 我____累，今天没休息好。
selfCheck.a: 我很累，今天没休息好。(Wǒ hěn lèi, jīntiān méi xiūxi hǎo.)

selfCheck.q: Fill the blank （老师 / 好看）: 他是一名中文____。
selfCheck.a: 他是一名中文老师。(Tā shì yì míng Zhōngwén lǎoshī.)

selfCheck.q: Fill the blank （吗 / 很）: 你饿____？
selfCheck.a: 你饿吗？(Nǐ è ma?)

selfCheck.q: Fill the blank （是 / 叫）: 请问，你____什么名字？
selfCheck.a: 请问，你叫什么名字？(Qǐngwèn, nǐ jiào shénme míngzi?)

selfCheck.q: Fill the blank （不 / 也）: 谢谢！____客气。
selfCheck.a: 谢谢！不客气。(Xièxie! Bú kèqi.)

selfCheck.q: Fill the blank （忙 / 渴）: 今天我很____，要做很多事。
selfCheck.a: 今天我很忙，要做很多事。(Jīntiān wǒ hěn máng, yào zuò hěn duō shì.)

selfCheck.q: Fill the blank （好吃 / 帅）: 这道菜很____，我很喜欢。
selfCheck.a: 这道菜很好吃，我很喜欢。(Zhè dào cài hěn hǎochī, wǒ hěn xǐhuan.)

selfCheck.q: Fill the blank （漂亮 / 累）: 她的衣服很____。
selfCheck.a: 她的衣服很漂亮。(Tā de yīfu hěn piàoliang.)

selfCheck.q: Fill the blank （是 / 很）: 我们____中国人。
selfCheck.a: 我们是中国人。(Wǒmen shì Zhōngguó rén.)

selfCheck.q: Fill the blank （是 / 饿）: 你____哪国人？
selfCheck.a: 你是哪国人？(Nǐ shì nǎ guó rén?)

selfCheck.q: Fill the blank （一起 / 见）: ____吃饭吧！
selfCheck.a: 一起吃饭吧！(Yìqǐ chī fàn ba!)

selfCheck.q: Correct the sentence: 我是中国的人。
selfCheck.a: 我是中国人。(Wǒ shì Zhōngguó rén.) — No 的 between 中国 and 人.

selfCheck.q: Correct the sentence: 一个星期是有七天。
selfCheck.a: 一个星期有七天。(Yí ge xīngqī yǒu qī tiān.) — No extra 是 before 有.

selfCheck.q: Correct the sentence: 我的生日是五月三天。
selfCheck.a: 我的生日是五月三号。(Wǒ de shēngrì shì wǔ yuè sān hào.) — Dates use 号, not 天.

selfCheck.q: Correct the sentence: 现在什么时候点？
selfCheck.a: 现在几点？(Xiànzài jǐ diǎn?)

selfCheck.q: Correct the sentence: 他是很饿了。
selfCheck.a: 他很饿了。(Tā hěn è le.) — or 他饿了。(Tā è le.) No 是 before an adjective.

selfCheck.q: Correct the sentence: 我们不很累。
selfCheck.a: 我们不太累。(Wǒmen bú tài lèi.) — "Not very" is 不太.

selfCheck.q: Correct the sentence: 你明天上班了吗？
selfCheck.a: 你明天上班吗？(Nǐ míngtiān shàngbān ma?) — 了 does not go with a future time.

selfCheck.q: Correct the sentence: 现在差八十点。
selfCheck.a: 现在差八分十点。(Xiànzài chà bā fēn shí diǎn.) — Say 分 for the minutes.

selfCheck.q: Correct the sentence: 他的电话号码是几？
selfCheck.a: 他的电话号码是多少？(Tā de diànhuà hàomǎ shì duōshao?) — Ask about a long number with 多少.

selfCheck.q: Correct the sentence: 我去西班牙一起朋友。
selfCheck.a: 我和朋友一起去西班牙。(Wǒ hé péngyou yìqǐ qù Xībānyá.)

selfCheck.q: Correct the sentence: 我们明天见下午。
selfCheck.a: 我们明天下午见。(Wǒmen míngtiān xiàwǔ jiàn.) — Time words go before the verb.

selfCheck.q: Correct the sentence: 这本书太好看吗？
selfCheck.a: 这本书好看吗？(Zhè běn shū hǎokàn ma?) — 太 does not go in a plain yes/no question.

selfCheck.q: Put in order: 你 / 高兴 / 认识 / 很
selfCheck.a: 认识你很高兴。(Rènshi nǐ hěn gāoxìng.)

selfCheck.q: Put in order: 了 / 对不起 / 太 / 我 / 忙
selfCheck.a: 对不起，我太忙了。(Duìbuqǐ, wǒ tài máng le.)

selfCheck.q: Put in order: 这个 / 好吃 / 不
selfCheck.a: 这个不好吃。(Zhège bù hǎochī.)

selfCheck.q: Put in order: 名字 / 人 / 那 / 叫 / 个 / 什么
selfCheck.a: 那个人叫什么名字？(Nàge rén jiào shénme míngzi?)

selfCheck.q: Put in order: 朋友 / 约翰 / 不是 / 我的 / 美国人
selfCheck.a: 我的朋友约翰不是美国人。(Wǒ de péngyou Yuēhàn bú shì Měiguó rén.)

selfCheck.q: Put in order: 妈妈 / 电话 / 没有 / 我
selfCheck.a: 我妈妈没有电话。(Wǒ māma méiyǒu diànhuà.)

selfCheck.q: Put in order: 二 / 月 / 今天 / 二十六 / 日 / 星期五
selfCheck.a: 今天二月二十六日，星期五。(Jīntiān èr yuè èrshíliù rì, xīngqīwǔ.)

selfCheck.q: Put in order: 叫 / 个 / 有 / 米科 / 朋友 / 我
selfCheck.a: 我有个朋友叫米科。(Wǒ yǒu ge péngyou jiào Mǐkē.)

selfCheck.q: Put in order: 吗 / 邮箱 / 这个 / 是 / 你的
selfCheck.a: 这个是你的邮箱吗？(Zhège shì nǐ de yóuxiāng ma?)

selfCheck.q: Put in order: 一 / 在 / 周 / 巴西 / 呆 / 我
selfCheck.a: 我在巴西呆一周。(Wǒ zài Bāxī dāi yì zhōu.) — I'm staying in Brazil for a week. 一周 = one week; the time span goes after the verb.

selfCheck.q: Put in order: 点 / 现在 / 几 / 了
selfCheck.a: 现在几点了？(Xiànzài jǐ diǎn le?)

selfCheck.q: Put in order: 星期二 / 我 / 下午 / 下班 / 三 / 点
selfCheck.a: 星期二我下午三点下班。(Xīngqī'èr wǒ xiàwǔ sān diǎn xiàbān.)

selfCheck.q: What's the difference between 想 and 要?
selfCheck.a: 想 = would like to (a wish): 我想喝茶。(Wǒ xiǎng hē chá.) 要 = order, need, have to, be going to: 我要一杯茶。(Wǒ yào yì bēi chá.) / 我要加班。(Wǒ yào jiābān.)

selfCheck.q: How do you say "I want to go too" with 也?
selfCheck.a: 我也想去。(Wǒ yě xiǎng qù.) — 也 goes after the subject and before the verb, never at the end.

selfCheck.q: How do you say "I don't feel like drinking coffee"?
selfCheck.a: 我不想喝咖啡。(Wǒ bù xiǎng hē kāfēi.) — use 不想; 不要 means "don't" or "don't want it".

notes.heading: From one person to two: 从, 比, 并
notes.body: 人 is a person seen from the side, and the first three characters in this lesson are built from two 人. In 从 one person follows the other; in 比 two people stand side by side, leaning the same way; in 并 two people are joined by a crossbar at the feet. The old dictionary 说文解字 puts it as 反从为比: mirror 从 and you get 比. Standing side by side leads naturally to comparing, so 比 means "to compare", while 并 means "to put together" and also strengthens a negative (并不是, "is actually not").

notes.heading: 从 — follow, obey, take part, "from"
notes.body: Because 从 shows one person following another, it first means "to follow", then "to obey" and "to take part in". In 一切从简 and 处罚从严 it means "to go by" a standard: keep everything simple, punish strictly. As a preposition it means "from": 从 marks the starting point and 到 marks the end point, as in 从这里到那里 ("from here to there").

notes.heading: 北 and 背 — back to back
notes.body: 北 shows two people back to back. Its first meaning was "back" (the spine): turning your back on someone means refusing to cooperate, and turning your back on the enemy in battle means running away, which is why 败北 means "to be defeated". Later 北 was used for the direction north, and the meaning "back" moved to 背, which adds the flesh component 月 below 北. 背 has two readings: bèi (noun) is the back of the body, and bēi (verb) means to carry something on your back.

notes.heading: 众 and 化 — three people, and one upside down
notes.body: 众 has three people, with a sun above them in the oldest forms; it was explained as people working under the sun, and it means "many" or "a crowd". In 化 one person stands upright beside another who is upside down, a picture of the sharpest change of all, life and death. Later 化 came to mean change of any kind, and as a suffix it works like "-ize": 电子化 (digitize), 西化 (Westernize). The line 天化，地育，人赞 gives each a job: Heaven brings change (化), Earth nurtures (育), and people lend a hand (赞).

notes.heading: Building words from characters you know
notes.body: Two single characters can join into a word, and the order matters: 天上 means "in the sky" but 上天 means "Heaven", and 下水 is "to get into the water" but 水下 is "underwater". Not every pair works: 北下 is not a word, and 上背 and 下背 are only informal short forms of 上背部 and 下背部. Real words you can build include 上火, 大夫, 水土, 文化, 天文 and 从众.

notes.heading: 一 and 不 — tone changes
notes.body: 不 is bù on its own and before a first, second or third tone (不吃 bù chī, 不行 bù xíng), but it becomes bú before a fourth tone (不去 bú qù, 不对 bú duì). 一 is yī when you count, say a date or end a word. Before a fourth tone it becomes yí (一次 yí cì); before a first, second or third tone it becomes yì (一起 yì qǐ, 一百 yì bǎi). The characters never change; only the pronunciation does.

selfCheck.q: Which character shows two people, one following the other, and what does it mean?
selfCheck.a: 从 (cóng) — to follow, to obey, to take part in; as a preposition, "from".

selfCheck.q: How do 比 and 并 differ in their pictures and meanings?
selfCheck.a: 比 = two people side by side, leaning the same way (to compare); 并 = two people joined by a crossbar (together, side by side; "not at all" before 不).

selfCheck.q: What picture is behind 北, and what are its two meanings?
selfCheck.a: Two people back to back — originally "the back" (hence 败北, "to be defeated"), and later "north" (北方 běifāng).

selfCheck.q: How do the two readings of 背 differ?
selfCheck.a: bèi (noun) = the back of the body, as in 后背; bēi (verb) = to carry on the back, as in 背包.

selfCheck.q: What do the pictures in 众 and 化 show?
selfCheck.a: 众 = three people (many people, a crowd); 化 = one person upright and one upside down (change, transformation).

selfCheck.q: How do you say "from morning till night" with 从…到…?
selfCheck.a: 从早到晚。(Cóng zǎo dào wǎn.)

selfCheck.q: How do you say "My back hurts" using 背疼?
selfCheck.a: 我背疼。(Wǒ bèi téng.)

selfCheck.q: How do you say "He is actually not a teacher" using 并不是?
selfCheck.a: 他并不是老师。(Tā bìng bú shì lǎoshī.)

selfCheck.q: Which tone do 不 and 一 take in 不去, 不吃, 一次 and 一起?
selfCheck.a: 不去 = bú qù (before a 4th tone); 不吃 = bù chī; 一次 = yí cì (before a 4th tone); 一起 = yì qǐ (before a 3rd tone).

selfCheck.q: What is the difference between 天上 and 上天?
selfCheck.a: 天上 (tiānshang) = in the sky; 上天 (shàngtiān) = Heaven, God.

notes.heading: 多 / 少 + verb — do more, do less
notes.body: Put 多 duō before a verb to say 'do more of it' and 少 shǎo before a verb to say 'do less of it'. This is the standard way to give health advice, and the verb is usually followed by 点 or by the thing itself, as in 多吃点蔬菜. Here 多 and 少 describe how much you DO something, so they are different from 很多 or 不少, which describe how many things there are.

notes.body: Chinese health advice loves to set a 多 phrase next to a 少 phrase in one breath: do more of the good thing, do less of the bad thing. The two halves usually have the same length and the same shape, which makes them easy to remember. Sometimes the second half has no action verb of its own, as in 少一个人在家 (be home alone less).

notes.heading: 对…过敏 and 对…好 — using 对
notes.body: The preposition 对 duì points at the thing that a state or effect is aimed at. So 对 + thing + 过敏 means 'allergic to it' and 对 + thing + 好 means 'good for it'. The whole 对 phrase goes BEFORE 过敏 or 好, and a degree word such as 有点儿, 很 or 不太 sits right in front of 过敏 or 好. The same frame also works with 有用 and 有效, as in 对过敏有效 'effective for allergies'.

notes.heading: 如果…就… — if…then…
notes.body: 如果 rúguǒ opens the condition ('if') and 就 jiù opens the result ('then'), right before the verb or adjective of the second clause. In everyday speech 如果 is often dropped, but 就 almost always stays. You can also line up two 如果 clauses to contrast the outcomes, as in the doctor's joke below.

notes.heading: 有用, 有效 and 没用 — does it work?
notes.body: 有用 yǒuyòng means useful or helpful, and 有效 yǒuxiào means effective, so both can say that a medicine works. 有用 is the general word that fits almost anything, while 有效 is more specific to results, especially for medicines and methods. The everyday opposite is 没用 méiyòng, 'useless' or 'it doesn't work'.

notes.heading: 吃药 or 喝汤? — choosing eat or drink
notes.body: Chinese uses 吃 chī ('eat') for taking medicine, so 吃药 is the normal way to say 'take medicine', even though it literally means 'eat medicine'. Liquids such as soup, water and alcohol go with 喝 hē ('drink'): 喝汤, 喝水, 喝酒. When one sentence has both, give each its own verb, as in the doctor's 喝一杯汤，吃过敏药. notes.heading: 都 — all / both, placed after what it sums up
notes.body: 都 dōu means "all" or "both" and goes right before the verb or adjective, after the subject — or after the whole list, as in 尺码和颜色都很好. It looks back at things already mentioned, even in the previous clause (我买了一些东西，都是你喜欢吃的), so they must come before it; unlike English "I like them both", 都 can't follow the object.

examples.chinese: 她和她丈夫都很喜欢猫。
examples.pinyin: Tā hé tā zhàngfu dōu hěn xǐhuan māo.
examples.english: She and her husband both love cats.

examples.pinyin: Zhīfùbǎo hé Wēixìn dōu kěyǐ.
examples.english: Alipay and WeChat are both fine.

notes.heading: 都…了 — already / even (with emphasis)
notes.body: Besides "all", 都 can mean "already" or "even". With 了 at the end it stresses that something is further along or more serious than expected: 都九月了 = "it's September already!". 已经 just states "already"; 都…了 adds surprise or a complaint. In 头发都白了, 都 means "all" and 了 marks the change; Chinese calls gray hair 白 (white).

notes.heading: 除了…以外，都… — except for
notes.body: 除了 chúle + the exception (+ 以外 yǐwài) + 都 means "apart from that, everything is…": the 除了 phrase is the odd one out. 以外 (or 之外) is optional and simply closes the 除了 phrase. Don't confuse this with 除了…还…, where 还 adds more: "besides this, also that".

examples.chinese: 除了写汉字以外，她的口语和听力都很棒。
examples.pinyin: Chúle xiě hànzì yǐwài, tā de kǒuyǔ hé tīnglì dōu hěn bàng.

notes.heading: 一定 / 不一定 — definitely / not necessarily
notes.body: 一定 yídìng goes before the verb or adjective and means "definitely": 一定会 + verb predicts, 一定 + adjective is a confident guess ("must be"), and 一定要 + verb is a firm "must". 不一定 bù yídìng means "not necessarily" — possible but not certain — and is NOT the same as 一定不, "definitely not".

notes.heading: 怕 — afraid of / can't stand
notes.body: 怕 pà means "to be afraid of" and takes a noun (怕狗), a verb phrase (怕坐飞机) or a clause (怕明天下雨 = "worried it will rain tomorrow"). Before 冷, 热 or 辣 it means "can't stand": 我怕冷 says you feel the cold easily. Negate with 不怕; say 别怕 for "don't be afraid". 害怕 hàipà also means "scared", but only 怕 works in 怕冷.

notes.heading: 好久没…了 and 一点儿也… — not for ages / not at all
notes.body: 好久没 + verb + 了 says you haven't done something for a long time; swap 好久 for a period to be exact (好几年没见面了 = "we haven't met for several years"). Here 没 and 了 appear together: the final 了 means "up to now", not "completed". For "not at all", use 一点儿也 (or 一点儿都) + 没 / 不 + verb or adjective: 你一点儿也没变 = "you haven't changed a bit".

notes.heading: …的时候 — when…, plus 没能 and 没有人
notes.body: A clause + 的时候 makes a "when…" phrase that normally comes before the main clause. 没能 + verb says you were not able to do something on that occasion, and 没有人 + verb means "nobody did it". After 我, 的 is dropped for close relationships and roles (我妻子, 我老板) but kept for ordinary possession (老板的办公室).

notes.heading: Measure words — 条, 张, 家, 道, 瓶
notes.body: Each noun takes its own measure word between the number (or 这 / 那) and the noun: 条 for long, narrow or flowing things (skirts, trousers, rivers), 张 for flat things (beds, tables, paper), 家 for businesses, 道 for dishes, 瓶 for bottles. 个 is the all-purpose fallback and works for 沙发 and 蛋糕.

selfCheck.q: What is the difference between 不一定 and 一定不?
selfCheck.a: 不一定 = "not necessarily" (it might or might not): 他不一定会来。(Tā bù yídìng huì lái.) 一定不 = "definitely not": 他一定不会来。(Tā yídìng bú huì lái.)

selfCheck.q: Where does 都 go in a sentence, and what must come before it?
selfCheck.a: Right before the verb or adjective, after the subject. It sums up what was already mentioned, so the things it refers to come first: 尺码和颜色都很好。(Chǐmǎ hé yánsè dōu hěn hǎo.)

selfCheck.q: What does 都…了 add compared with 已经…了?
selfCheck.a: Emphasis or surprise: 都九月了！(Dōu jiǔyuè le!) = "It's September already!", while 已经九月了 simply states it.

notes.heading: 在…呢 — action in progress
notes.body: Put 在 before a verb to say an action is happening right now, and add 呢 at the end for a lively, chatty tone; 正在 stresses "at this very moment". To ask what someone is doing, say 你在做什么呢？ — or the more casual 你在干什么呢？ and 你在干吗呢？ — and answer with 我在 + activity. Make it negative with 没在 rather than 不在. When the sentence also needs a place, put 在 before the place and 在 again before the verb: 孩子们在学校在踢球。

notes.heading: 都 — all and already
notes.body: 都 goes right before the verb and has two jobs. Meaning "all" or "both", it sums up the people or things named before it, so the subjects come first: 她和孩子都喜欢吃苹果。 Followed by a time or a number plus 了, it means "already" and hints that it is later, or more, than expected: 都十一点了。

notes.heading: 给 — to or for someone
notes.body: As a verb, 给 means "to give": 给 + person + thing. As a preposition it names the person an action is aimed at or done for, and that 给-phrase goes before the verb. So where English says "call Mom", Chinese says 给妈妈打电话 — literally "to Mom, make a call". Phone and message verbs such as 打电话 and 发消息 almost always take it.

notes.heading: 得 (děi) — have to, and 不用 — don't have to
notes.body: 得 děi goes before a verb and means "have to" or "need to". It is informal, and it is often the reason you give for turning something down: 我得去机场接朋友。 The usual negative is 不用 búyòng, "no need to" or "don't have to". Don't confuse 得 děi with 得 de, which comes after a verb and links it to a description (睡得很晚), or with 能, which says you are able or allowed to.

notes.heading: 再 — again (not yet happened)
notes.body: 再 zài means "again" or "once more" for something that has not happened yet — a wish, a request or a plan. It goes before the main verb, after a modal such as 能, 要 or 想: Subject + (modal verb) + 再 + verb. It sounds exactly like 在, the "in progress" or "at a place" word, so check the character. For a repetition that has already happened, Chinese uses 又 instead.

notes.heading: Phone calls and making plans
notes.body: Open a phone call with 喂 (wèi, also read wéi), say who you are with 我是…, and ask 有事吗？ if you want to know why someone is calling. selfCheck.q: How do you say "I'm jogging right now" with 正在 and 呢?
selfCheck.a: 我正在跑步呢。(Wǒ zhèngzài pǎobù ne.)

selfCheck.q: How do you say "They aren't watching TV"? Which word goes before 在 in the negative?
selfCheck.a: 他们没在看电视。(Tāmen méi zài kàn diànshì.) Use 没 before 在, not 不.

selfCheck.q: How do you say "The children are playing soccer at school" when the sentence has both a place and an action in progress?
selfCheck.a: 孩子们在学校在踢球。(Háizimen zài xuéxiào zài tī qiú.)

selfCheck.q: How do you say "I phoned my mom yesterday" with 给?
selfCheck.a: 昨天我给妈妈打电话了。(Zuótiān wǒ gěi māma dǎ diànhuà le.) The 给-phrase goes before the verb 打.

selfCheck.q: When does 都 mean "all", and when does it mean "already"?
selfCheck.a: 都 + verb = "all": 我们都去过北京。(Wǒmen dōu qù guo Běijīng.) 都 + time + 了 = "already": 都十一点了。(Dōu shíyī diǎn le.)

selfCheck.q: How do you say "I have to go to the airport to pick up a friend" — and "I don't have to"?
selfCheck.a: 我得去机场接朋友。(Wǒ děi qù jīchǎng jiē péngyou.) / 我不用去机场接朋友。(Wǒ búyòng qù jīchǎng jiē péngyou.)

selfCheck.q: 能 or 得? 他发烧了，不___去上班了。 / 我没有钱了，下午___去银行。
selfCheck.a: 他发烧了，不能去上班了。(Tā fāshāo le, bù néng qù shàngbān le.) / 我没有钱了，下午得去银行。(Wǒ méiyǒu qián le, xiàwǔ děi qù yínháng.) 能 = can (circumstances allow); 得 = have to.

selfCheck.q: How do you politely turn down an invitation and suggest another time?
selfCheck.a: 不行啊，我得去机场接朋友。我们下次再约。(Bùxíng a, wǒ děi qù jīchǎng jiē péngyou. Wǒmen xiàcì zài yuē.)

selfCheck.q: How do you ask "Can you say it one more time?" — and why is it 再, not 在?
selfCheck.a: 你能再说一遍吗？(Nǐ néng zài shuō yí biàn ma?) 再 means "again" for something that has not happened yet; 在 marks an action in progress or a place.

notes.heading: 比 — A is more … than B
notes.body: Put 比 between the two things you compare and end with an adjective: A + 比 + B + adjective. Never put 很, 非常 or 太 before that adjective. To say the gap is large, add 多了 or 得多 after the adjective. When the adjective is 多 itself you get 多多了, "far more".

notes.heading: 没有 — A is not as … as B
notes.body: The normal way to deny a 比 sentence is to swap 比 for 没有: A + 没有 + B + adjective means "A is not as … as B". Keep the adjective bare, with no 很 or 太 in front of it. The negative usually starts from the weaker side, so 哥哥比妹妹高 turns into 妹妹没有哥哥高.

notes.heading: 更, 最 and 极了 — degree words
notes.body: 更 means "even more" and is the degree word that fits inside a 比 sentence: 北京比伦敦更热. 最 means "the most": it can stand directly before a noun in set max-and-min terms (最高气温, 最低气温, 最快速度), while an ordinary noun needs 的 (最贵的衣服). 极了 comes AFTER an adjective or a psychological verb (喜欢, 高兴, 激动, 难过, 害怕, 讨厌, 满意, 生气) and means "extremely".

notes.heading: 多 — approximate numbers
notes.body: 多 after a number means "and a bit more". After a ROUND number (十, 二十, 两百, 两千 …) it sits before the measure word; after any other number it follows the measure word. With 十 the order changes the meaning: 十多岁 is 11–19 years old, but 十岁多 is just over 10.

notes.heading: 又, 再 and 还 — again, still
notes.body: 又 and 再 both translate as "again", but they look in different directions. 又 reports a repetition that has already happened, so the sentence usually ends in 了 (他今天又迟到了). 再 is for a repetition that has not happened yet — a plan, a wish or a request (明天再开会吧). 还 is different again: before a negative it means "still" or "not yet" (春天还没到).

notes.heading: 还…呢 — "even!" and "not bad"
notes.body: Subject + 还 + verb phrase + 呢 stresses that something is impressive, special, unexpected or hard to achieve — "I even …!". It is often used to show off or to drop a surprising extra detail. Don't confuse it with 还没…呢, which means "not yet". On its own, 还 + 可以 / 不错 / 行 / 过得去 is a modest way to say "not bad".

notes.heading: Complaining and showing concern
notes.body: Complaints get their strength from 真, 太…了, 有点儿 and 极了, and 又…了 adds the annoyance of "not again!". Concern is shown by asking 怎么办 ("what shall we do?") or by turning a good situation round with 不过 ("but …") to flag a worry. Use 听说 to pass on what you have heard and 是吗？ to check it.

notes.heading: Talking about weather and seasons
notes.body: Ask 现在是什么季节？ for the season, 天气怎么样？ for the weather and 气温多少度？ for the temperature. Answer with a season, a weather word and a number of degrees; 大概 adds "roughly" and 零下 means below zero. Spring is 暖和, summer 热, autumn 凉快 and winter 冷, while 不冷也不热 describes a mild day. 习惯 says you have got used to a climate: 我们习惯了.

selfCheck.q: What is the difference between 十多岁 and 十岁多?
selfCheck.a: 十多岁 (shí duō suì) = 11–19 years old; 十岁多 (shí suì duō) = just over 10.

notes.heading: The legend of Chang'e — part 1: the hero and the suns
notes.body: The legend of 嫦娥 (Cháng'é) and 后羿 (Hòuyì), a married couple, is the story behind the festival. Long ago ten suns burned the earth; Hou Yi, a master archer (神射手), shot down nine of them to save humankind (人类), which made him a hero (英雄). Read the eight example sentences in this note and the next two in order to retell the whole legend.

examples.chinese: 嫦娥和后羿是一对好夫妻。
examples.pinyin: Cháng'é hé Hòuyì shì yí duì hǎo fūqī.
examples.english: Chang'e and Hou Yi are a good married couple.

examples.chinese: 很久以前，天上有十个太阳。
examples.pinyin: Hěn jiǔ yǐqián, tiānshang yǒu shí ge tàiyáng.
examples.english: Long ago there were ten suns in the sky.

examples.chinese: 后羿是神射手，他射下了九个太阳，救了人类。
examples.pinyin: Hòuyì shì shénshèshǒu, tā shè xià le jiǔ ge tàiyáng, jiù le rénlèi.
examples.english: Hou Yi was a master archer; he shot down nine suns and saved humankind.

notes.heading: The legend of Chang'e — part 2: the elixir
notes.body: The Jade Emperor (玉帝) gives Hou Yi a magic elixir (仙丹), and Hou Yi asks Chang'e to look after it (保管). A villain (坏人) tries to force her to hand it over (交出). She does not agree (同意), so she swallows the elixir herself to keep it out of his hands.

examples.chinese: 玉帝给后羿一颗仙丹，后羿请嫦娥保管。
examples.pinyin: Yùdì gěi Hòuyì yì kē xiāndān, Hòuyì qǐng Cháng'é bǎoguǎn.
examples.english: The Jade Emperor gave Hou Yi an elixir pill, and Hou Yi asked Chang'e to keep it safe.

examples.chinese: 坏人想拿仙丹，嫦娥不同意交出来。
examples.pinyin: Huàirén xiǎng ná xiāndān, Cháng'é bù tóngyì jiāo chūlái.
examples.english: A villain wanted the elixir, but Chang'e would not agree to hand it over.

examples.chinese: 为了不让坏人拿到仙丹，嫦娥自己吃了。
examples.pinyin: Wèile bú ràng huàirén nádào xiāndān, Cháng'é zìjǐ chī le.
examples.english: So that the villain would not get the elixir, Chang'e ate it herself.

notes.heading: The legend of Chang'e — part 3: flying to the moon
notes.body: Chang'e flies (飞) up to the moon (月亮) and lives in a palace (宫殿) with a little rabbit (小兔子) for company (陪伴). Hou Yi runs after her but cannot catch up (追不上), and he misses (思念) her every day. This is why people look at the moon and think of absent family at the festival.

examples.chinese: 嫦娥飞到月亮上，小兔子陪伴她。
examples.pinyin: Cháng'é fēi dào yuèliang shang, xiǎo tùzi péibàn tā.
examples.english: Chang'e flew to the moon, and the little rabbit kept her company.

examples.chinese: 后羿追不上她，每天都思念她。
examples.pinyin: Hòuyì zhuībushàng tā, měi tiān dōu sīniàn tā.
examples.english: Hou Yi could not catch up with her, and missed her every day.

notes.heading: 中秋节 — the Mid-Autumn Festival
notes.body: The festival falls on the 15th day of the 8th month of the lunar calendar (农历八月十五), when the moon is at its roundest. Families reunite (团圆), admire the moon (赏月) and eat mooncakes (月饼), whose round shape stands for the full moon and for a complete family. Dates written with 农历 are lunar dates, so the festival moves around in the Gregorian calendar (usually September or early October).

notes.heading: Festival greetings
notes.body: The standard greeting is 中秋节快乐！ ("Happy Mid-Autumn Festival!"). To wish someone well, put 祝 (zhù) in front; 祝…团圆 wishes a family a happy reunion. Reply to a greeting by repeating it.

examples.english: Happy Mid-Autumn Festival!

examples.chinese: 祝你和家人中秋节快乐！
examples.pinyin: Zhù nǐ hé jiārén Zhōngqiūjié kuàilè!
examples.english: Wishing you and your family a happy Mid-Autumn Festival!

examples.pinyin: Zhù nǐmen quán jiā tuányuán!
examples.english: Wishing your whole family a happy reunion!

notes.heading: 让, 不让 and 为了 — story patterns
notes.body: 让 means "to let" or "to have someone do something"; 不让 means "not to let / to prevent". 为了 introduces a purpose clause ("in order to / for the sake of") and usually comes at the start of the sentence. In the legend, Chang'e eats the elixir 为了不让坏人拿到 it — the two patterns stack.

examples.english: The teacher has us read the text.

notes.heading: 拿到 and 追不上 — result complements
notes.body: A verb plus 到 or 上 says the action reached its goal: 拿到 means "got hold of" and 追上 means "caught up with". Put 不 between the verb and 上 for "cannot": 追不上 means "can't catch up with" (the 不 is read short and light here). With 得 instead you say "can": 追得上. Negate a plain 到 result with 没(有): 没拿到.
